questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not have any "crucial" aspects in choosing my destination. However I found it important that the courses I was going to attend were courses that I would actually enjoy. After reading about UoE's (many) interesting courses I just became more certain that UoE was the right choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do believe that it is important to do some research about the accommodation opportunities in your exchange country when you are choosing a destination. My overall experience would have been a lot better if my accommodation, apartment (private leased), had been better. Coming from Copenhagen where a lot of the apartments are modern and renovated, I found it difficult to live in an apartment with mold, mouse and drafts. The apartment did not function as my "safe" space and a place were I could relax after a long day.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Do your research from home and you will be fine. The UoE were very helpful in many ways! Great communication and they are doing their best in taking good care of their students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not need any crucial assistance when I arrived. I was also lucky to have co-students from UCPH with me so we helped each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I did not need any "important" assistance but I know that the UoE is very helpful if you need any help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find an apartment. I leased an apartment with my co-students from UCPH through a private landlord.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You should try and find an apartment well in advance. Not one month before you leave (as we did but that was also because of some missing email about being accepted). 
Ask to see the apartment before you are renting it!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not understand why housing is not guaranteed for single semester students. Besides economic, social and moving to a different country, the stress would have been reduced knowing I was guaranteed housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I have expressed in my previously answers, UoE are very helpful and the registration process, due to Covid-19, was online making it very flexible for students.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to send my boarding pass upon arriving to prove I were present at the host country.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The CAHSS Visiting Student Office is very helpful if you need any help!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful as I was accepted for the courses I had applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are in doubt just ask your host university - write an email, book an appointment. They are helpful and do only wish the best for their exchange students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As a third year student and having to do first year courses were great. I got to refresh what I have previously learned and at the same time in English.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was suitable for someone which mother tongue is not English. Challenging, but not too difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Compared to UCPH the lectures were recorded 👌. I also had the opportunity to attend seminars to discuss texts and the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Social Anthropology 1B Anthropology Matters
Evidence, Politics and Policy
Data Literacy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It depends on what you are interested in. Read the course catalogue as UoE has a lot of great courses!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I do not think I encountered any unexpected costs but it is important to have a saving in case you face any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think the food was a bit expensive compared to Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I did not attend any, I did see a lot of opportunities at the host institution.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know there were a lot of social activities available for students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not anticipate in any but I would recommend doing it if need a social group with same interests.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city and the highlands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Denmark is ahead in many aspects and I found the difficult that a lot of the way things are done in Scotland are done differently.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Come to the seminars

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences to be challenging. The culture is different and that is an experience.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated how kind, helpful and open the scottish people are compared to people in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Do your research about the destination especially the housing (and of course the university)!
2. Have a saving so you can have fun in the weekends as the Erasmus grant will not get you far 🥴
3. Be prepared for better online opportunities

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have fun!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That what I thought I could not handle, I managed!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The personal challenges I have faced but in a good way. While the exchange may not have been the best, I have learned a lot and appreciate things in a completely different way now.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: DO IT! ❤️

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
